prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: background illustration for Counting Sheep iPhone Home hero, intended to have the EXISTING Ollie sprite composited on top in code. Input 1 is the exact existing brown-and-white border collie illustration: STYLE reference only, do NOT paint the dog in this background. Input 2 is the existing farm pixel-art world: palette and cozy world reference. Generate a 1536 by 1024 landscape home interior at dusk, a welcoming modest farmhouse living room, front-on low three-quarter game camera. Blend the app's soft paper-cut painterly textures with deliberate lightly pixel-stepped silhouettes of its environments, not photorealistic, not 3D. A small warmly glowing table lamp and simple wooden door on the left, window showing lavender twilight and distant hills on the right, a small soft armchair near the far wall, muted sage green walls and honey-brown timber floor. Keep the central foreground rug and floor broad, EMPTY, uncluttered, and evenly lit so a 2D standing or lying collie can occupy the center lower 60 percent of the picture. Warm welcoming home emotion, quiet nighttime lighting, soft cream/sage/muted gold/lavender, avoid black shadows and oversaturated orange. Fill entire canvas with illustration. No characters, no dogs, no people, no sheep, no text, no UI, no frames, no decorative sparkles, no watermark. Props all at back or edges, no foreground obstruction. This is a single hero background, not a whole app screenshot.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: EXTREMELY MINIMAL backdrop for a Counting Sheep home hero, with only TWO small isolated illustrated home ornaments. Reference image 1: existing Ollie mascot identity/art STYLE only, do NOT draw dog. Reference image 2: game environment texture STYLE only, do NOT draw room or landscape. Canvas 1536x1024 landscape. The entire canvas background is exactly flat near-black #101611. NO wall texture, no floor, no horizon, no room, no vignette, no full scene. Draw only (1) a small simple warm table lamp with a short stem and a tiny oval base at x22% y48%, maximum 13% canvas width and 25% height; lamp has soft cream fabric shade, muted honey wood stem, very restrained warm light inside shade, no radiating light background. (2) a small square wooden-framed window at x76% y32%, max 17% canvas width and 24% height, dark lavender dusk sky and a tiny crescent moon, no curtains, no view of hills. These TWO ornaments convey home with almost all the canvas empty. Use soft paper-cut hand painted game illustration, subtly pixel-stepped edges consistent with reference world. Keep center and lower half completely empty for Ollie to be composited later. Small, understated, muted sage/honey/lavender, not glossy, not 3D. No rug, no chair, no plants, no books, no shelves, no door, no decorative stars, no text, no UI, no dog, no people, no watermark. A minimalist symbolic home, NOT an illustrated room. Ensure all unpainted pixels are flat #101611.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: transparent 2D animation SPRITE SHEET for the existing Counting Sheep mascot Ollie. Input image 1 is the exact model-sheet identity and seated home pose. Input image 2 is reference for this SAME dog's lying-down proportions and soft painted paper texture. Generate a single 1536x1024 PNG sprite sheet: EXACTLY 4 equal columns by 3 equal rows, 12 separate frames in left-to-right top-to-bottom order. No gutters, no borders, no text, no numbers. Each cell is 384x341 pixels. Transparent alpha background, no checkerboard painted in, no floor, no shadows, no props. One complete Ollie per cell, no cropping. Keep exact brown-white border collie identity, purple eyes, white forehead blaze/muzzle/chest/paws, white-tipped brown tail, triangular ears, friendly expression, paper-cut soft brush texture, NOT realistic fur, NOT 3D, NOT a different dog. Consistent camera: three-quarter FRONT, body faces slightly right, eyes toward viewer; don't rotate to profile. Keep SAME head scale and physical size throughout, same ground contact baseline at 90% of each cell height, centered at 50% horizontally. Sitting dog occupies 80% cell height; lying dog naturally shorter but NOT scaled down. Action is a relaxed comical flop then return, NOT sad or injured. Frame 1: original upright sitting relaxed, ears up. Frame 2: ears tuck BACK warmly, eyes soften, torso still seated. Frame 3: ears back, lean chest forward, front elbows begin bend. Frame 4: chest drops quickly toward rug, front paws sliding forward, hindquarters rolling gently one side. Frame 5: soft flop landed, chest and belly on ground, paws extended, head still above paws. Frame 6: chin rests on white front paws, sleepy content eyes half closed, tucked ears. Frame 7: same lying pose, eyes closed, content, tiny exhale in body ONLY, no symbols. Frame 8: same lying pose, eyes open, ears beginning lift, head raises. Frame 9: lifts chest pushing up on front legs, hindquarters low. Frame 10: hindquarters rise, almost standing on four paws, same camera. Frame 11: standing on all four paws, ears upright. Frame 12: returns to upright seated resting pose matching frame 1 EXACTLY. Sheet must be machine-sliceable uniform cell grid. It is an animation keyframe asset study; prioritize character identity, ear-fold and flop mechanics, and aligned scale over decoration.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Input image is the EDIT TARGET: the 12-pose Ollie sprite-sheet animation study just generated. Change ONLY the background. Replace the ENTIRE white/light-grey checkerboard with one perfectly uniform flat solid color #101611 (RGB 16,22,17). There must be NO checkerboard, NO transparency simulation, no grid, no outlines or shadows added. Preserve every dog's exact pose, facial markings, purple eyes, ear shapes, white fur, brown fur, placement, size, scale, and texture unchanged, and keep the same 1536x1024 canvas. Do not change any dog pixels, do not rearrange cells, do not crop, do not rescale or invent extra frames. The dogs should stand against a completely flat near-black green background. No text or watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, a 12-pose Ollie animation study on dark background. Image 2 is the original character model, identity reference only. Correct ONLY the EAR GEOMETRY of the tucked-ear poses (frames 2 through 9, reading left to right then next row). The user explicitly rejected the current sideways 'airplane ears'. They need anatomically recognizable EARS FOLDED BACK, not spread sideways. Rotate each triangular ear at its base toward the BACK OF THE SKULL, so the ear tips point rearward AWAY from the viewer and are mostly OCCLUDED behind the head. From this three-quarter front camera, tucked ears should look like a very small rounded brown fold at the upper rear contour of the skull; almost no pink inner ear is visible. The lateral head silhouette must NOT have any outward-pointing triangular ears or wings. Keep the ear folds INSIDE the maximum width of the cheek silhouette, flat against the skull. For frames 2-7 both ears fully pinned gently BACK in a friendly relaxed manner, like a happy dog greeting its owner then relaxing, not frightened. Frame 8 still largely pinned back as head rises. Frame 9 ears just starting to lift backward/upward, not sideways. Frames 1,10,11,12 retain their original upright ears. Preserve all 12 poses, all body positions, purple eyes, white blaze, brown and white fur markings, texture, frame placements and 1536x1024 canvas from image1. Do NOT change the face or enlarge/shrink heads. Preserve near-black green background #101611. No text, no arrows, no anatomy diagrams, no new frames. The key correction must be unmistakable: back-swept/hidden ears, NO outward lateral triangles.

Use case: identity-preserve. EDIT this exact original Ollie illustration. Change ONLY his upright ears to HAPPY DOG 'SEAL EARS': both ears swept tightly backward, pressed flat along the back of the skull so they almost DISAPPEAR from this front three-quarter view. This is NOT floppy ears, NOT ears folded forward over the forehead, NOT ear flaps dangling beside temples, NOT airplane ears pointing left/right. The crown of the head becomes a smooth rounded brown dome, with only a TINY curved brown ridge on the rear-left contour indicating the back of a folded ear. No pink inner-ear surfaces visible. Ear tips tucked BEHIND the head, occluded by head, not hanging down in front and not sticking out sideways. Keep all other features EXACTLY: same seated pose, purple eyes, brown-white markings, white forehead blaze, muzzle, tail, paws, facing slightly right, soft paper texture, size. Ollie has a calm affectionate expression; eyes not wide with fear. On flat solid #101611 near-black green background. Single full-body character centered, 1024x1024. No room, no scene, no symbols, no text, no extra poses. Key visual: almost earless rounded seal-head silhouette because both ears are physically swept backwards and hidden behind skull.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image1 is the EDIT TARGET: 12-pose Ollie animation sheet. Image2 is the CORRECT TUCKED-EAR reference: its rounded skull with ears swept behind the head, almost invisible, NOT floppy side flaps. Transfer ONLY that ear treatment to poses 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 of image1 (left-to-right top-to-bottom). In those poses remove the lateral triangle/flap silhouettes and show both ears tightly swept backwards and OCCLUDED behind the skull exactly like image2. Smooth rounded crown, only tiny brown ridge behind back of skull, no pink inner-ear, no hanging flaps on temples, no sideways points. Pose9 may start lifting ears a tiny amount backward. Poses1,10,11,12 KEEP original upright ears. Keep each head size, white blaze, eye expression, body geometry, pose, paws and placement the same as image1. Keep original smooth painted paper texture, don't add heavy mottling. Canvas1536x1024 exactly; same 4columns3rows layout. Uniform background #101611. No outlines, grid, labels, text or new shadows. Maintain the action: seated -> ears tightly back -> lean -> flop -> chin down -> rest eyes close -> head up -> push up -> standing -> seated. THIS IS EAR CORRECTION ONLY, do not copy image2's enlarged body or change framing.

Edit the cartoon Ollie in reference image 1, changing ONLY his ears. References 2 and 3 show the real border collie whose ear structure should guide this change. Reference 2 is the indoor photo: note the long narrow triangular ear structure, natural slight asymmetry, one ear more upright and the other relaxed. Reference 3 is the outdoor photo (photo is rotated): look specifically at the DOG looking up; its ears lie back but remain visibly projecting, shaped ears, with recognizable bases and pointed tips. Translate that real anatomy into the existing simple paper-cut cartoon style. This is a single full-body seated test pose for a relaxed ears-back animation. Keep both ears clearly present, of the original character's length and substance, but rotate them BACK at the base and lower their angle, so the pointed tips trail backward behind the crown toward the upper neck. Preserve a subtle natural asymmetry. The near ear should show a visible tapered folded silhouette above and behind the cheek, the far ear slightly higher and foreshortened. Do NOT flatten them into an earless round head; do NOT make rounded spaniel/Labrador flaps dangling forward; do NOT make symmetrical sideways airplane triangles. Use the real dog in the supplied photos to determine the geometry rather than inventing a different ear type. Keep original cartoon face shape, large purple eyes, white blaze and muzzle, brown-white body, seated pose and proportions, original happy mild expression and brush texture; don't alter the eyes or make the dog photorealistic. Don't copy people, furniture, screens, documents or outdoor scenery from photos. Single full-body character centered on solid #101611 near-black green, square canvas. No text, no comparison panels, no extra objects. Prefer an understated believable backward ear movement over an exaggerated caricature.

Use case: identity-preserve. Edit reference image1 (the ORIGINAL seated cartoon Ollie) to make one tongue-out welcome pose. Image2 is a real dog's warm tongue-out expression reference only, not a subject/style replacement. Preserve the original cartoon's body proportions, sitting posture, brown-white markings, purple eyes, white blaze, tail and original pointed upright ear silhouettes EXACTLY. Do NOT use the previously generated flattened or sideways ears. Change ONLY mouth expression: a slightly open smiling muzzle, a small soft rose-pink rounded tongue hanging out naturally, about one nose-width wide and 1.5 nose-heights long below the mouth, not all the way down chest. Tiny warm dark mouth interior, no prominent teeth, no drool. Maintain the restrained affectionate expression seen in the real dog photo, no exaggerated grin, not frantic panting. Keep original paper-cut soft painted texture, don't make detailed realistic fur or a new angular mosaic texture. Full body with all paws visible, same original framing, 1024x1024 square on solid dark #101611. No text, no props, no human or bedroom from reference photo. This is a single greeting key pose that will briefly appear before a separate flop animation.
